summary: fetch-page-assets ships obfuscated Ethereum dead-drop RCE loader in babel.config.cjs and a fake.woff2
details: babel.config.cjs contains a two-line valid babel preset followed by a large obfuscator.io-transformed payload (numeric string table, index rotator, unicode-escaped API names) that queries Ethereum JSON-RPC endpoints (eth.blockscout.com, 1rpc.io/eth, eth.drpc.org, ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io) for the most recent outgoing transaction from the hardcoded sender address 0xa322E5f3D311D3080e6f0121063e9aDC2490Ef1a, decodes the recipient-address bytes into two IPv4 dead-drop C2 hosts, fetches XOR-encrypted second-stage code from those hosts at /0x/cls and /0x/ls, then executes the decrypted output via eval() and via a detached child_process.spawn('node', ['-e',...], {detached: true}).unref(). public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2 is not a font file — it is plain JavaScript implementing the identical Ethereum-dead-drop, XOR-decrypt, eval/spawn loader with the same sender address and the same /0x/cls and /0x/ls C2 paths, staged as an apparent static asset. The loader fires whenever Babel loads this file, giving whoever controls the Ethereum address arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
